title: SRE cross-team tactical calendar & decision canvas — Reliability Program SLO rollout (2026)
content:
Status: draft -> in_review
Owners: Marcus Chen (SRE lead), Lina Gomez (Product), Tom Reynolds (Serving Runtime), Priya Shah (Platform Eng), Jamal Rivers (Customer Success)

Purpose
- Create a pragmatic, time-boxed tactical plan for rolling out the Reliability Program SLOs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Surface decisions early via a decision canvas so leadership and cross-functional partners can align on risk tradeoffs and rollout pace.

High-level objectives (what success looks like)
1) Agree and publish a canonical set of customer-impacting SLOs for the first wave (text-generation API, chat routes) by end of Q1 2026.
2) Implement monitoring, alerting, and runbooks so that 95% of P1 incidents have a clear on-call play within 15 minutes.
3) Demonstrate a 10–15% reduction in Sev2 surface area from baseline via targeted mitigations and routing fallbacks by the end of the first 12-week sprint.
4) Delivery of per-route SLO dashboards in Console for top-10 paid routes.

Success metrics (measurable)
- SLO coverage: % of customer traffic covered by an active SLO (target: 60% by week 12).
- Time-to-detection: median MTTD for Sev1/Sev2 incidents (target: <5m for Sev1, <15m for Sev2).
- Runbook completeness score (manual checklist): goal 90% of SLOs have runbooks with play, rollback, and stakeholder list.
- Customer impact: number of customer-facing incidents/month (target: reduce by 10% over baseline).

SLOs proposed for wave 1 (draft)
- Availability SLO: 99.9% successful 2xx responses for text-gen (30d rolling).
- Latency P50/P95: P95 for small requests (<512 tokens) <250ms for hosted tier; P95 <500ms for dedicated baseline.
- Error budget burn policy: automated fallback to next-compatible model variant when burn >20% in last 24h.
(These are intentionally conservative for wave 1 — open to product input for finer gradations by route)

12-week tactical calendar (high level)
Weeks 1–2: alignment & data collection
- Workshop with Product + Runtime to finalize candidate SLO definitions (REL-342).
- Export traffic slices and baseline metrics per route.
- Quick wins list: prefix caching config, retry/backoff standardization.
Weeks 3–4: monitoring & runbook skeletons
- Build metric aggregations in observability (Console pilot dashboards).
- Draft per-route runbook templates (owner, thresholds, rollback).
- Stakeholder signoff: Product, Security, CS.
Weeks 5–7: implement mitigations & alerting
- Implement early routing fallbacks and quantization recommendation flags for dedicated clusters.
- Add automated alerts for error-budget thresholds; smoke test.
- Run tabletop incident drill (simulate model OOM / high latency).
Weeks 8–10: evaluate and iterate
- Measure SLO coverage and error budget usage across traffic.
- Tune batching and cache windows based on real traffic.
- Finalize Console dashboard views for top routes.
Weeks 11–12: rollout & handoff
- Canary SLO enforcement on low-traffic routes.
- Handoff to on-call + publish runbooks and escalate matrix.
- Exec summary and next-phase planning.

Decision canvas (to unblock fast):
- Decision: Aggressive vs conservative latency targets for hosted API P95.
  - Criteria: user-visible degradation tolerance, engineering cost of infra changes, rollback complexity.
  - Recommendation: conservative first-pass (higher P95) + explicit timeline to tighten after 8 weeks.
- Decision: Automated model fallback behaviour when error budget near burn.
  - Criteria: fidelity of fallback, cost delta, customer transparency.
  - Recommendation: default to automated fallback to verified compatible variant with logging and customer-visible incident note.
- Decision: Which routes are wave 1 (top-lines)
  - Criteria: revenue impact, frequency, support noise.
  - Recommendation: pick top-10 paid routes + 5 high-noise internal routes.

RACI (top-level)
- Define SLOs: R=SRE, A=Product, C=Serving Runtime, I=Security/CS.
- Implement instrumentation/alerts: R=Platform Eng, A=SRE, C=Observable Eng.
- Runbooks: R=SRE, A=Customer Success, C=Product.
- Console dashboarding + UX: R=Console Eng, A=Product, C=SRE.
(Keep owners tight: we will list route-level owners in separate sheet)

Integration touchpoints (must-haves)
- Serving Runtime: kernel selection and quantization flags for fallbacks (PR: infra#987).
- Console: route-level SLO widgets and error budget visualizations.
- Customer Success: incident comms templates and account-level SLO reports.
- Security/Compliance: logging retention and PII scoping for runbooks.

Deployment and release checklist (minimal)
- Metrics validated on staging for 48h with synthetic traffic.
- Alerts reviewed and noise-minimized (alert fatigue check).
- Runbook complete and tested in a tabletop.
- Stakeholders notified, escalation chain confirmed.

Known risks & mitigations
- Noise/false positives from naive thresholds -> Mitigation: use percentile + rolling windows; sanity-check thresholds on sample traffic.
- Customer confusion over fallback model behavior -> Mitigation: CS + Product create FAQ + tenant-level opt-out.
- Infra cost spike due to aggressive retries -> Mitigation: cap retries + rate-limiter per tenant.

Open questions (needs input)
- Should we classify SLOs by customer tier (hosted free vs paid vs dedicated)? (Action: Product to recommend classification by week 2).
- Is automated fallback allowed for private deployments without explicit customer opt-in? (Action: Legal/Security to weigh in).
- Exact latency targets for dedicated clusters — Product and SRE to align by week 3.

Meeting cadence and recommended attendees
- Weekly sync (30m) — SRE, Product PO, Serving Runtime tech lead, Platform Eng rep, Console PM.
- Bi-weekly leadership checkpoint (45m) — Directors from SRE, Product, Infra, CS.
- Incident tabletop (week 6) — cross-functional drill with blameless postmortem.

Immediate next steps (this doc owner)
- Book workshop with Product + Runtime (weeks 0–1) — owner: Marcus (by 2025-11-10).
- Export baseline metrics by route and attach to REL-342 (owner: Lina, due 2025-11-14).
- Draft runbook template and circulate for review (owner: Tom, due 2025-11-21).

Notes to self / working items (rough)
- Keep per-route owner mapping in a sheet (not here).
- Pull sample traffic distribution for P95 calculation; avoid tail-loss bias.
- Consider adding a lightweight customer-facing SLO status page for enterprise customers.

Appendix: quick references
- Jira: REL-342 (SLO definitions), REL-358 (alerting infra), REL-412 (runbook templates).
- PR: infra#987 (fallback routing prototype).
- Confluence: SLO-Runbook draft (link above).

Unresolved: we still need legal signoff on customer notification copy for automatic fallbacks (owner: Evelyn Park).

----
This is intentionally a tactical, usable canvas for the next 12 weeks. Use comments in this doc for items you disagree with; aim to converge on decisions in the week 1 workshop.
summary: Tactical 12-week plan, decision canvas, owners, measurable success metrics, meetings, and next steps for rolling out Reliability Program SLOs across product, serving runtime, and platform.
